subject.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes

question: What level of content continuity should be required before an update may retain the default automatic approval path?
rationale: The automatic policy intentionally avoids a redundant prompt, but the data-loss fix needs a durable trust boundary for destructive replacements; choosing that boundary changes operator workflow and cannot be inferred safely from tests.

options.title: Require substantial continuity
options.body: Use a meaningful overlap or replacement threshold and force low-continuity updates pending while ordinary edits remain automatic.

options.title: Gate every update
options.body: Require explicit approval for every update proposal, maximizing safety at the cost of reverting the recent automatic workflow for updates.

options.title: Keep auto after parsing
options.body: Apply all structurally valid proposals automatically and rely on generation prompts plus rollback, accepting that plan-like bodies can still replace skills.

recommendation.title: Require substantial continuity
recommendation.body: Use a meaningful overlap or replacement threshold and force low-continuity updates pending while ordinary edits remain automatic.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and live-verified the current automatic approval contract that this decision would narrow.
